You are urban_comet97, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
10 agents form one group, and you work with brisk_harbor75, early_island22, gentle_otter27, jolly_ember22, pale_kettle84, pale_lantern48, rapid_thistle87, sandy_walnut42, zesty_lantern63. Each agent works in its own sandbox, on its
own git repository. Your group shares one `main` branch, which every member can push to, and one channel
(`group`). Work together with your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to
coordinate and share helpful findings.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is your group's final score: the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on `main` at
the end. Every agent receives the same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents announce what they are exploring, building, or have found,
and ask each other questions. Typical posts include a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a finding (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), a proposal for how to organize the work, or a question.
- `post` publishes a message to `group`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, and any unopened posts that mention you, one line each
  (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a post's number shows its full text, with its
  pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished, with a pointer, then go back
  to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main` does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve as
  many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. <collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

## Task context
Build a new implementation from scratch that matches the behavior of the reference executable.
The executable is located at `/opt/reference/executable`.
You also have access to the existing documentation.

## Your task
Implement a program whose externally observable behavior matches the reference executable.
Write it in **Python 3.10**.
- Its documentation is in `/workspace` (README and other files). There is no source code and no internet.
- Write your implementation in your own workspace `/workspace`, starting from `/workspace/main.py`.
  You may add more Python modules next to it. **Standard library only.**
- `/workspace/compile.sh` is already provided: at evaluation time it turns `main.py` into the program under
  test. **Do not run it in your workspace.** Test your code with `python3 main.py ...`.
- Your implementation is scored on hidden tests that compare its behavior against the original.

**Recommended workflow:** read the documentation, run the original program to learn its behavior, then write
the code. Start writing `main.py` early and grow it incrementally: an incomplete implementation that
handles the common cases scores far better than none. After each change, run your code against the
original to check it. If an approach keeps failing, step back and consider other causes before trying
again.
I’ll first inspect the bundled docs and probe the executable’s main CLI paths, then I’ll share the discovered feature map with the team and implement a useful slice in `main.py`.

{"status":"fulfilled","value":{"chunk_id":"9fb9a9","wall_time_seconds":0.000008763,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":5834,"output":"# Minify [![API reference](https://img.shields.io/badge/godoc-reference-5272B4)](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2?tab=doc) [![Go Report Card](https://goreportcard.com/badge/github.com/tdewolff/minify)](https://goreportcard.com/report/github.com/tdewolff/minify) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/tdewolff/minify/branch/master/graph/badge.svg?token=Cr7r2EKPj2)](https://codecov.io/gh/tdewolff/minify) **[Online demo](https://go.tacodewolff.nl/minify)** if you need to minify files *now*. **[Binaries](https://github.com/tdewolff/minify/releases) of CLI for various platforms.** See [CLI](https://github.com/tdewolff/minify/tree/master/cmd/minify) for more installation instructions. **[Windows binary from scoop](https://scoop.sh/#/apps?q=minify)** install with `scoop install main/minify` **[Python bindings](https://pypi.org/project/tdewolff-minify/)** install with `pip install tdewolff-minify` **[JavaScript bindings](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tdewolff/minify)** install with `npm i @tdewolff/minify` **[.NET bindings](https://github.com/JKamsker/NMinify)** install with `Install-Package NMinify` or `dotnet add package NMinify`, thanks to Jonas Kamsker for the port --- *Did you know that the shortest valid piece of HTML5 is `x`? See for yourself at the [W3C Validator](http://validator.w3.org/)!* Minify is a minifier package written in [Go][1]. It provides HTML5, CSS3, JS, JSON, SVG and XML minifiers and an interface to implement any other minifier. Minification is the process of removing bytes from a file (such as whitespace) without changing its output and therefore shrinking its size and speeding up transmission over the internet and possibly parsing. The implemented minifiers are designed for high performance (see https://github.com/privatenumber/minification-benchmarks where this library is (one of) the fastest JS minifiers). The core functionality associates mimetypes with minification functions, allowing embedded resources (like CSS or JS within HTML files) to be minified as well. Users can add new implementations that are triggered based on a mimetype (or pattern), or redirect to an external command (like ClosureCompiler, UglifyCSS, ...). ### Sponsors #### SiteGround [![SiteGround](https://www.siteground.com/img/downloads/siteground-logo-black-transparent-vector.svg)](https://www.siteground.com/) Thank you SiteGround for having sponsored this project for many years! Their contribution is invaluable for code maintenance and improvements. If you are in need of professional web hosting, I can highly recommend their products. #### Requesting sponsors I'm actively looking for support in the form of donations or sponsorships to keep developing this library and highly appreciate any gesture. Please see the Sponsors button in GitHub for ways to contribute, or contact me directly. #### Table of Contents - [Minify](#minify) - [Prologue](#prologue) - [Installation](#installation) - [API stability](#api-stability) - [Testing](#testing) - [Performance](#performance) - [HTML](#html) - [Whitespace removal](#whitespace-removal) - [CSS](#css) - [JS](#js) - [Comparison with other tools](#comparison-with-other-tools) - [Compression ratio (lower is better)](#compression-ratio-lower-is-better) - [Time (lower is better)](#time-lower-is-better) - [JSON](#json) - [SVG](#svg) - [XML](#xml) - [Usage](#usage) - [New](#new) - [From reader](#from-reader) - [From bytes](#from-bytes) - [From string](#from-string) - [To reader](#to-reader) - [To writer](#to-writer) - [Middleware](#middleware) - [Custom minifier](#custom-minifier) - [Mediatypes](#mediatypes) - [Examples](#examples) - [Common minifiers](#common-minifiers) - [External minifiers](#external-minifiers) - [Closure Compiler](#closure-compiler) - [UglifyJS](#uglifyjs) - [esbuild](#esbuild) - [Custom minifier](#custom-minifier-example) - [ResponseWriter](#responsewriter) - [Templates](#templates) - [FAQ](#faq) - [License](#license) ### Roadmap - [ ] Use ASM/SSE to further speed-up core parts of the parsers/minifiers - [x] Improve JS minifiers by shortening variables and proper semicolon omission - [ ] Speed-up SVG minifier, it is very slow - [x] Proper parser error reporting and line number + column information - [ ] Generation of source maps (uncertain, might slow down parsers too much if it cannot run separately nicely) - [ ] Create a cmd to pack webfiles (much like webpack), ie. merging CSS and JS files, inlining small external files, minification and gzipping. This would work on HTML files. ## Prologue Minifiers or bindings to minifiers exist in almost all programming languages. Some implementations are merely using several regular expressions to trim whitespace and comments (even though regex for parsing HTML/XML is ill-advised, for a good read see [Regular Expressions: Now You Have Two Problems](http://blog.codinghorror.com/regular-expressions-now-you-have-two-problems/)). Some implementations are much more profound, such as the [YUI Compressor](http://yui.github.io/yuicompressor/) and [Google Closure Compiler](https://github.com/google/closure-compiler) for JS. As most existing implementations either use JavaScript, use regexes, and don't focus on performance, they are pretty slow. This minifier proves to be that fast and extensive minifier that can handle HTML and any other filetype it may contain (CSS, JS, ...). It is usually orders of magnitude faster than existing minifiers. ## Installation Make sure you have [Git](https://git-scm.com/) and [Go](https://golang.org/dl/) (1.18 or higher) installed, run ``` mkdir Project cd Project go mod init go get -u github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2 ``` Then add the following imports to be able to use the various minifiers ``` go import ( "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2" "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2/css" "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2/html" "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2/js" "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2/json" "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2/svg" "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2/xml" ) ``` You can optionally run `go mod tidy` to clean up the `go.mod` and `go.sum` files. See [CLI tool](https://github.com/tdewolff/minify/tree/master/cmd/minify) for installation instructions of the binary. ### Docker If you want to use Docker, please see https://hub.docker.com/r/tdewolff/minify. ```bash $ docker run -it tdewolff/minify --help ``` ## API stability There is no guarantee for absolute stability, but I take issues and bugs seriously and don't take API changes lightly. The library will be maintained in a compatible way unless vital bugs prevent me from doing so. There has been one API change after v1 which added options support and I took the opportunity to push through some more API clean up as well. There are no plans whatsoever for future API changes. ## Testing For all subpackages and the imported `parse` package, test coverage of 100% is pursued. Besides full coverage, the minifiers are [fuzz tested](https://github.com/tdewolff/fuzz) using [github.com/dvyukov/go-fuzz](http://www.github.com/dvyukov/go-fuzz), see [the wiki](https://github.com/tdewolff/minify/wiki) for the most important bugs found by fuzz testing. These tests ensure that everything works as intended and that the code does not crash (whatever the input). If you still encounter a bug, please file a [bug report](https://github.com/tdewolff/minify/issues)! ## Performance The benchmarks directory contains a number of standardized samples used to compare performance between changes. To give an indication of the speed of this library, I've ran the tests on my Thinkpad T460 (i5-6300U quad-core 2.4GHz running Arch Linux) using Go 1.15. ``` name time/op CSS/sample_bootstrap.css-4 {"status":"fulfilled","value":{"chunk_id":"3f8558","wall_time_seconds":0.00000417,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":719,"output":"## CSS

Minification typically shaves off about 10%-15%. This CSS minifier will _not_ do structural changes to your stylesheets. Although this could result in smaller files, the complexity is quite high and the risk of breaking website is high too.

The CSS minifier will only use safe minifications:

- remove comments and unnecessary whitespace (but keep `/*! ... */` which usually contains the license)
- remove trailing semicolons
- optimize `margin`, `padding` and `border-width` number of sides
- shorten numbers by removing unnecessary `+` and zeros and rewriting with/without exponent
- remove dimension and percentage for zero values
- remove quotes for URLs
- remove quotes for font families and make lowercase
- rewrite hex colors to/from color names, or to three digit hex
- rewrite `rgb(`, `rgba(`, `hsl(` and `hsla(` colors to hex or name
- use four digit hex for alpha values (`transparent` → `#0000`)
- replace `normal` and `bold` by numbers for `font-weight` and `font`
- replace `none` → `0` for `border`, `background` and `outline`
- lowercase all identifiers except classes, IDs and URLs to enhance gzip compression
- shorten MS alpha function
- rewrite data URIs with base64 or ASCII whichever is shorter
- calls minifier for data URI mediatypes, thus you can compress embedded SVG files if you have that minifier attached
- shorten aggregate declarations such as `background` and `font`

It does purposely not use the following techniques:

- (partially) merge rulesets
- (partially) split rulesets
- collapse multiple declarations when main declaration is defined within a ruleset (don't put `font-weight` within an already existing `font`, too complex)
- remove overwritten properties in ruleset (this not always overwrites it, for example with `!important`)
- rewrite properties into one ruleset if possible (like `margin-top`, `margin-right`, `margin-bottom` and `margin-left` → `margin`)
- put nested ID selector at the front (`body > div#elem p` → `#elem p`)
- rewrite attribute selectors for IDs and classes (`div[id=a]` → `div#a`)
- put space after pseudo-selectors (IE6 is old, move on!)

There are a couple of comparison tables online, such as [CSS Minifier Comparison](http://www.codenothing.com/benchmarks/css-compressor-3.0/full.html), [CSS minifiers comparison](http://www.phpied.com/css-minifiers-comparison/) and [CleanCSS tests](http://goalsmashers.github.io/css-minification-benchmark/). Comparing speed between each, this minifier will usually be between 10x-300x faster than existing implementations, and even rank among the top for minification ratios. It falls short with the purposely not implemented and often unsafe techniques.

Options:

- `Precision` number of significant digits to preserve for numbers, `0` means no trimming
- `Version` CSS version to use for output, `0` is the latest

const patch="*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/css_min.py
+"""Small standalone CSS minifier used by the CLI implementation."""
+import re
+
+
+def _comments(s):
+    out=[]; i=0; quote=None
+    while i<len(s):
+        c=s[i]
+        if quote:
+            out.append(c)
+            if c=='\\' and i+1<len(s): i+=1; out.append(s[i])
+            elif c==quote: quote=None
+            i+=1; continue
+        if c in "'\"": quote=c; out.append(c); i+=1; continue
+        if s.startswith('/*',i):
+            j=s.find('*/',i+2)
+            if j<0: break
+            comment=s[i:j+2]
+            if comment.startswith('/*!'): out.append(comment)
+            i=j+2; continue
+        out.append(c); i+=1
+    return ''.join(out)
+
+
+def _numbers(s, precision):
+    def sub(m):
+        n=m.group()
+        try:
+            v=float(n)
+            if precision: v=float(format(v, f'.{precision}g'))
+            z=format(v,'.15g')
+            if z.startswith('0.'): z=z[1:]
+            elif z.startswith('-0.'): z='-'+z[2:]
+            return z
+        except ValueError: return n
+    return re.sub(r'(?<![\w#-])[-+]?(?:\d*\.\d+|\d+\.?\d*)(?:[eE][-+]?\d+)?',sub,s)
+
+
+def minify_css(text, precision=0, version=0):
+    s=_comments(text)
+    # Whitespace can be dropped at punctuation; keep descendant combinators and
+    # spaces between identifiers. Strings are protected by the scanner below.
+    out=[]; i=0; quote=None; pending=False
+    for c in s:
+        if quote:
+            out.append(c)
+            if c==quote: quote=None
+            elif c=='\\': pass
+            continue
+        if c in "'\"":
+            if pending and out and (out[-1].isalnum() or out[-1] in '_-'):
+                out.append(' ')
+            pending=False; quote=c; out.append(c); continue
+        if c.isspace(): pending=True; continue
+        if c in '{}:;,>+~()':
+            while out and out[-1]==' ': out.pop()
+            out.append(c); pending=False
+        else:
+            if pending and out and out[-1] not in '{:;,>+~(' and c not in '})],;:': out.append(' ')
+            pending=False; out.append(c)
+    s=''.join(out)
+    s=re.sub(r';}', '}',s)
+    s=re.sub(r'(?i)\b(font-weight\s*:\s*)bold\b',r'\g<1>700',s)
+    s=re.sub(r'(?i)\b(font-weight\s*:\s*)normal\b',r'\g<1>400',s)
+    s=re.sub(r'(?i)\b(?:margin|padding|border-width)\s*:\s*([^;}]+)',lambda m:m.group(0),s)
+    s=re.sub(r'(?<![\w.])(?:0)(?:px|em|rem|%|pt|cm|mm|in|pc|ex|ch|vh|vw)\b','0',s,flags=re.I)
+    s=re.sub(r'(?i)#([0-9a-f])\1([0-9a-f])\2([0-9a-f])\3\b',r'#\1\2\3',s)
+    s=re.sub(r'(?i)#ff0000\b','red',s); s=re.sub(r'(?i)#ffffff\b','#fff',s); s=re.sub(r'(?i)#000000\b','#000',s)
+    s=_numbers(s,precision)
+    # Four-value shorthand reductions.
+    def shorthand(m):
+        p=m.group(1); vals=m.group(2).split()
+        while len(vals)>1 and vals[-1]==vals[1]: vals.pop()
+        if len(vals)==3 and vals[0]==vals[2]: vals.pop()
+        if len(vals)==2 and vals[0]==vals[1]: vals.pop()
+        return p+':'+ ' '.join(vals)
+    s=re.sub(r'(?i)\b(margin|padding|border-width):([^;}]+)',shorthand,s)
+    return s
+
*** End Patch";
text(await tools.apply_patch(patch))

import json
import re
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation, ROUND_HALF_UP

_NUM = re.compile(r'-?(?:0|[1-9]\d*)(?:\.\d+)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?')


def _number(token, precision):
    try:
        d = Decimal(token)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return token
    if not d.is_finite() or d == 0:
        return '0' if d == 0 else token
    if precision and len(d.normalize().as_tuple().digits) > precision:
        shift = d.adjusted() - precision + 1
        d = d.quantize(Decimal(1).scaleb(shift), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    tup = d.normalize().as_tuple()
    digits = ''.join(map(str, tup.digits)) or '0'
    exponent = tup.exponent
    sign = '-' if tup.sign else ''
    # Exponent notation avoids leading zeroes and trailing fractional zeroes.
    if exponent >= 0:
        return sign + digits + ('e' + str(exponent) if exponent else '')
    # For ordinary-size values, use a decimal point when it is no longer.
    point = len(digits) + exponent
    if 0 < point <= len(digits):
        plain = sign + digits[:point] + ('.' + digits[point:] if point < len(digits) else '')
    elif point <= 0:
        plain = sign + '0.' + '0' * (-point) + digits
    else:
        plain = sign + digits + '0' * (point - len(digits))
    compact_exp = exponent
    compact = sign + digits + 'e' + str(compact_exp)
    return compact if len(compact) < len(plain) else plain



def minify_json(text, keep_numbers=False, precision=0):
    """Compact JSON while preserving string spelling and optionally number spelling."""
    json.loads(text)  # Match parser errors before emitting any output.
    out = []
    i = 0
    in_string = False
    escaped = False
    while i < len(text):
        c = text[i]
        if in_string:
            out.append(c)
            if escaped:
                escaped = False
            elif c == "\\":
                escaped = True
            elif c == '"':
                in_string = False
            i += 1
        elif c == '"':
            in_string = True
            out.append(c)
            i += 1
        elif c.isspace():
            i += 1
        elif c == '-' or c.isdigit():
            m = _NUM.match(text, i)
            if m:
                token = m.group()
                out.append(token if keep_numbers else _number(token, precision))
                i = m.end()
            else:
                out.append(c)
                i += 1
        else:
            out.append(c)
            i += 1
    return ''.join(out)

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+import sys, os, re, json
+from pathlib import Path
+from json_min import minify_json
+from css_min import minify_css
+from jsmin import minify_js
+from svg_min import minify_svg
+from xml_min import minify as minify_xml
+
+TYPES = [('asp','text/asp'),('css','text/css'),('ejs','text/x-ejs-template'),('gohtml','text/x-go-template'),('handlebars','text/x-handlebars-template'),('htm','text/html'),('html','text/html'),('js','application/javascript'),('json','application/json'),('mjs','application/javascript'),('mustache','text/x-mustache-template'),('php','application/x-httpd-php'),('rss','application/rss+xml'),('svg','image/svg+xml'),('tmpl','text/x-template'),('webmanifest','application/manifest+json'),('xhtml','application/xhtml+xml'),('xml','text/xml')]
+LIST='\n'.join(f'{a:<12} {b}' for a,b in TYPES)+'\n'
+
+def html_min(s, keep_comments=False, keep_quotes=False, keep_tags=False, keep_end=False, keep_ws=False, **kw):
+    if not keep_comments: s=re.sub(r'<!--(?!\[if|#).*?-->', '', s, flags=re.S)
+    s=re.sub(r'>\s+<','><',s)
+    s=re.sub(r'[\t\r\n ]+',' ',s).strip()
+    s=re.sub(r'\s*([=<>])\s*',r'\1',s)
+    if not keep_quotes:
+        s=re.sub(r'="([\w./:#-]+)"',r'=\1',s)
+    if not keep_tags:
+        s=re.sub(r'</?(?:html|head|body)\b[^>]*>','',s,flags=re.I)
+    if not keep_end:
+        s=re.sub(r'</(?:li|p|tr|td|th|option)>','',s,flags=re.I)
+    return s
+
+def minify(data, typ, opts):
+    t=typ.lower().split(';')[0].strip()
+    aliases={'css':'text/css','html':'text/html','htm':'text/html','xhtml':'application/xhtml+xml','js':'application/javascript','javascript':'application/javascript','json':'application/json','svg':'image/svg+xml','xml':'text/xml'}
+    t=aliases.get(t,t)
+    if t=='text/css': return minify_css(data,opts.get('css_precision',0),opts.get('css_version',0))
+    if t in ('application/json','text/json','application/manifest+json','text/manifest+json') or t.endswith('+json') or t.endswith('/json'):
+        return minify_json(data,opts.get('json_keep_numbers',False),opts.get('json_precision',0))
+    if t in ('application/javascript','text/javascript','text/ecmascript','application/ecmascript','text/x-javascript'):
+        return minify_js(data,opts.get('js_keep_var_names',False),opts.get('js_precision',0))
+    if t=='image/svg+xml': return minify_svg(data,opts.get('svg_keep_comments',False),opts.get('svg_precision',0))
+    if t in ('text/xml','application/xml','application/rss+xml','application/xhtml+xml') or t.endswith('+xml'):
+        return minify_xml(data,opts.get('xml_keep_whitespace',False))
+    if t=='text/html' or t.startswith('text/x-') or t in ('text/asp','application/x-httpd-php','application/xhtml+xml') or t.endswith('html'):
+        return html_min(data,**opts)
+    raise ValueError('minifier does not exist for mimetype')
+
+def main():
+    args=sys.argv[1:]
+    if '--help' in args or '-h' in args:
+        print('Usage: executable [options] inputs...\nUse --type to specify stdin format; --list and --version show supported types/version.')
+        return 0
+    if '--version' in args: print('minify 2.24.13'); return 0
+    if '--list' in args or '-l' in args: sys.stdout.write(LIST); return 0
+    opts={}; typ=None; output=None; inplace=False; quiet=False; positional=[]
+    names={'--html-keep-comments':'html_keep_comments','--html-keep-quotes':'html_keep_quotes','--html-keep-document-tags':'html_keep_tags','--html-keep-end-tags':'html_keep_end','--html-keep-whitespace':'html_keep_ws','--json-keep-numbers':'json_keep_numbers','--svg-keep-comments':'svg_keep_comments','--xml-keep-whitespace':'xml_keep_whitespace','--js-keep-var-names':'js_keep_var_names'}
+    i=0
+    while i<len(args):
+        a=args[i]
+        if a in ('--type','--mime','-o','--output','--css-precision','--css-version','--json-precision','--js-precision','--js-version','--svg-precision'):
+            if i+1==len(args): print(f'ERROR: flag needs an argument: {a}',file=sys.stderr); return 1
+            v=args[i+1]; i+=1
+            k={'--type':'type','--mime':'type','-o':'output','--output':'output','--css-precision':'css_precision','--css-version':'css_version','--json-precision':'json_precision','--js-precision':'js_precision','--js-version':'js_version','--svg-precision':'svg_precision'}[a]
+            if k=='type':typ=v
+            elif k=='output':output=v
+            else:

+                except: opts[k]=0
+        elif a.startswith('--type='): typ=a.split('=',1)[1]
+        elif a.startswith('--mime='): typ=a.split('=',1)[1]
+        elif a.startswith('--output=') or a.startswith('-o='): output=a.split('=',1)[1]
+        elif a in names: opts[names[a]]=True
+        elif a in ('-i','--inplace'): inplace=True
+        elif a in ('-q','--quiet'): quiet=True

+        else: positional.append(a)
+        i+=1
+    if not positional:

"""Conservative JavaScript tokenizer/minifier used by the CLI implementation."""
import re
from js_mangle import mangle

_TOKEN = re.compile(r'''\s+|//[^\r\n]*|/\*[\s\S]*?\*/|(?:'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*'|"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"|`(?:\\.|[^`\\])*`)|(?:\d+(?:\.\d*)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?)|(?:[$\w]+)|(?:===|!==|>>>|==|!=|<=|>=|=>|\+\+|--|&&|\|\||\?\?|\+=|-=|\*=|/=|\*\*|\.\.\.|<<|>>)''')
_WORD = re.compile(r'^[\w$]')

def _regex_literal_end(source, pos):
    i=pos+1; in_class=False; escaped=False
    while i<len(source):
        c=source[i]
        if c in '\r\n': return None
        if escaped: escaped=False
        elif c=='\\': escaped=True
        elif c=='[': in_class=True
        elif c==']': in_class=False
        elif c=='/' and not in_class:
            i+=1
            while i<len(source) and source[i].isalpha(): i+=1
            return i
        i+=1
    return None

def minify_js(source, options=None):
    options = options or {}
    source = re.sub(r'<!--[\s\S]*?-->', '', source)
    def opt(name, default=None):
        return options.get(name, options.get(name.replace('-', '_'), default))
    tokens = []
    pos = 0
    while pos < len(source):
        if (source[pos]=='/' and not source.startswith(('//','/*'),pos)
                and (not tokens or tokens[-1] in ('=', '(', '[', '{', ',', ':', ';', '!', '?', '&&', '||', '??', '=>', 'return', 'throw', 'case', 'delete', 'void', 'typeof', 'yield', 'await'))):
            end=_regex_literal_end(source,pos)
            if end is not None:
                tokens.append(source[pos:end]); pos=end; continue
        m = _TOKEN.match(source, pos)
        if not m:
            tokens.append(source[pos]); pos += 1; continue
        t = m.group(0); pos = m.end()
        if t.isspace() or t.startswith('//') or (t.startswith('/*') and not t.startswith('/*!')):
            continue
        if t in ('true', 'false'):
            nxt=source[pos:].lstrip()
            prev=tokens[-1] if tokens else ''
            is_key=(prev in ('.','?.') or (prev in ('{',',') and (nxt.startswith(':') or nxt.startswith('('))))
            if not is_key:
                t='!0' if t=='true' else '!1'
        elif re.fullmatch(r'\d+(?:\.\d*)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?', t):
            precision = int(opt('js-precision', 0) or 0)
            if precision:
                try:
                    t = format(float(t), f'.{precision}g')
                    t = re.sub(r'e([+-])0+(\d+)', r'e\1\2', t)
                except (ValueError, OverflowError):
                    pass
        tokens.append(t)
    for i, token in enumerate(tokens):
        if len(token) >= 2 and token[0] in ('"', "'") and token[-1] == token[0]:
            key=token[1:-1]
            if (re.fullmatch(r'[$A-Za-z_][\w$]*',key) and i+1<len(tokens) and tokens[i+1]==':'
                    and i>0 and tokens[i-1] in ('{',',')):
                tokens[i]=key
    tokens=mangle(tokens, bool(opt('js-keep-var-names', False)))
    # Concatenate adjacent plain string literals when doing so is unambiguous.
    i = 0
    while i + 2 < len(tokens):
        a, op, b = tokens[i:i+3]
        if (op == '+' and len(a) >= 2 and len(b) >= 2 and a[0] == a[-1] and b[0] == b[-1]
                and a[0] in "'\"" and b[0] in "'\""
                and not any(c in a[1:-1] + b[1:-1] for c in ('\\', a[0], b[0]))):

    ident = re.compile(r'^[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*$')
    atom = re.compile(r'^(?:[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*|\d+(?:\.\d*)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?|!0|!1|true|false|null|undefined|(?:\"[^\"\\]*\"|\'[^\'\\]*\'))$')

                and ident.fullmatch(tokens[i+6]) and tokens[i+7] == '=' and atom.fullmatch(tokens[i+8])

    # Turn a guarded pair of single call statements into a conditional expression.
    def close_at(seq, start, left, right):
        depth=0
        for j in range(start, len(seq)):
            if seq[j] == left: depth += 1
            elif seq[j] == right:
                depth -= 1
                if depth == 0: return j
        return -1
    def call_stmt(seq):
        if not seq: return False
        depth=0; saw_call=False
        for j,t in enumerate(seq):
            if t == '(': depth+=1; saw_call=True
            elif t == ')':
                depth-=1
                if depth<0:return False
            elif t in ('{','}',';'):

        return depth==0 and saw_call
    i=0
    while i < len(tokens):
        if tokens[i] != 'if' or i+1>=len(tokens) or tokens[i+1] != '(':
            i+=1; continue
        cp=close_at(tokens,i+1,'(',')')
        if cp<0 or cp+1>=len(tokens) or tokens[cp+1]!='{': i+=1; continue
        b1=close_at(tokens,cp+1,'{','}')
        if b1<0: i+=1; continue
        cond=tokens[i+2:cp]; yes=tokens[cp+2:b1]
        if b1+1>=len(tokens) or tokens[b1+1]!='else' or b1+2>=len(tokens) or tokens[b1+2]!='{':
            if yes and yes[0] in ('return','var','let','const'):
                tokens[i:b1+1]=['if']+tokens[i+1:cp+1]+yes
                i=max(0,i-1)
            else: i+=1
            continue
        b2=close_at(tokens,b1+2,'{','}')
        if b2<0: i+=1; continue
        no=tokens[b1+3:b2]
        if yes and no and yes[0]=='return' and no[0]=='return' and cond:
            y=yes[1:-1] if yes[-1:]==[';'] else yes[1:]
            n=no[1:-1] if no[-1:]==[';'] else no[1:]
            tokens[i:b2+1]=['return']+cond+['?']+y+[':']+n+[';']
            i=max(0,i-1)
        elif call_stmt(yes) and call_stmt(no) and cond:
            if yes[-1:]==[';']: yes=yes[:-1]
            if no[-1:]==[';']: no=no[:-1]
            tokens[i:b2+1]=cond+['?']+yes+[':']+no
            i=max(0,i-1)
        else: i+=1
    out = ''
    prev = ''
    for t in tokens:
        if prev and ((_WORD.match(prev[-1:]) and _WORD.match(t[:1])) or (prev[-1:] in '+-' and t[:1] == prev[-1:]) or (prev[-1:] == '/' and t.startswith('/'))):
            out += ' '
        out += t
        prev = t
    # Safe punctuation cleanup: remove semicolons immediately before a closing brace.
    out = re.sub(r';+}', '}', out)
    # Collapse simple conditional expression statements.
    ternary = re.compile(r'\bif\(([^(){}]+)\)\{([^{};]+)\}else\{([^{};]+)\}')
    def ternary_expr(m):
        if re.match(r'(?:return|throw|break|continue|var|let|const)\b', m.group(2)) or re.match(r'(?:return|throw|break|continue|var|let|const)\b', m.group(3)):
            return m.group(0)
        return m.group(1)+'?'+m.group(2)+':'+m.group(3)
    out = ternary.sub(ternary_expr, out)
    guarded = re.compile(r'\bif\(([^(){}]+)\)\{([^{}]+)\}(?!\s*else)')
    def guarded_expr(m):
        statements=[x for x in m.group(2).split(';') if x]
        if not statements or any(re.match(r'(?:return|throw|break|continue|var|let|const)\b', x) for x in statements):
            return m.group(0)
        expr=statements[0] if len(statements)==1 else '('+','.join(statements)+')'
        if re.match(r'^[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*(?:(?:\.[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)|(?:\[[^\]]+\]))*(?:\+=|-=|\*=|/=|%=|&=|\|=|\^=|<<=|>>>=|>>=|&&=|\|\|=|\?\?=|=(?!=|>))',expr):
            expr='('+expr+')'
        return m.group(1)+'&&'+expr
    out = guarded.sub(guarded_expr, out)
    # Remove a final semicolon (the parser's output convention).
    out = re.sub(r';+$', '', out)
    out = re.sub(r'\(([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\)=>', r'\1=>', out)
    return out
